record.paper_title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
record.original_question: Network monitoring can mean either monitoring propagation on a fixed network or monitoring a network that itself changes over time. What are the precise connections between these network-surveillance problems, disease transmission, and epidemic thresholds in temporal networks?

evidence.quote: Both problems have important connections with disease transmission and epidemic thresholds, and studying these connections is still an open question.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a temporal network represented as a time-indexed sequence of graphs G_t = (V, E_t) for t in a discrete or continuous time domain T, where V is a fixed set of n nodes and E_t ⊆ V × V is the set of edges active at time t. On such a structure, consider a stochastic spreading process (e.g., a susceptible–infected–susceptible (SIS) or susceptible–infected–recovered (SIR) model) with per-contact infection rate β and recovery rate μ, where infections may propagate only along edges that are active at the moment of contact. The epidemic threshold is the critical value of β/μ (or analogous control parameter) above which the expected fraction of infected nodes remains bounded away from zero in the large-time and/or large-n limit.

Two distinct network-surveillance problems are defined on this setting:
(i) Surveillance of propagation on a fixed network: given a static graph G = (V, E), select a subset S ⊆ V (sensors) of bounded size that minimizes the expected detection time, or maximizes the probability of detection, of a spreading process initiated at an unknown source.
(ii) Surveillance of a changing network: given the temporal network {G_t}, select (possibly time-varying) sensors S_t ⊆ V to detect either anomalous changes in the network structure itself or propagation processes whose dynamics interact with the changing topology.

Problem. Establish precise mathematical relationships between problems (i) and (ii) and the epidemic threshold of the underlying spreading process on the temporal network. Specifically:
(a) Derive quantitative bounds linking optimal sensor placements (and their detection-time guarantees) in problems (i) and (ii) to spectral or combinatorial quantities that determine the epidemic threshold on {G_t}.
(b) Identify conditions under which solving (i) is equivalent to, reducible to, or strictly easier/harder than solving (ii), in terms of the temporal-network parameters that govern the threshold.
(c) Characterize how the epidemic threshold itself can be inferred or estimated from observations available through optimal surveillance schemes of types (i) and (ii).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction concerning the connections between network-surveillance problems, disease transmission, and epidemic thresholds on temporal networks. No definitive resolution establishing the precise mathematical connections appears in the literature; subsequent reviews and works on temporal-network epidemics continue to treat these as ongoing research challenges.

status_evidence.title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Both problems have important connections with disease transmission and epidemic thresholds, and studying these connections is still an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The connections between network-surveillance problems and epidemic thresholds on temporal networks are stated as open.
